Looking at the H&E section, the tissue is not a full‑thickness, predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate. The majority of the field (especially the right and central areas) is made up of large cells with abundant eosinophilic (pink) cytoplasm and round, vesicular nuclei — i.e., epithelial/neoplastic cells, **not** lymphocytes. The small, dark blue lymphocytes are present but are concentrated focally (left side and upper region) rather than forming a dense infiltrate that spans the entire epithelial thickness.

So a predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate through the full thickness is **not** a feature of this image, and your answer of "no" is correct.
